;;;; game-2048.lisp

(in-package :game-2048)

(defun copy-board (board)
  (let ((new (make-array '(4 4) :initial-element 0)))
    (dotimes (r 4 new)
      (dotimes (c 4)
        (setf (aref new r c) (aref board r c))))))

(defun make-empty-board ()
  (make-array '(4 4) :initial-element 0))

(defun slide-row (row)
  "Slide ROW toward its first element, merging once per tile.
Returns a fresh list of the same length and the points gained."
  (let ((tiles (remove 0 row))
        (out '())
        (score 0))
    (loop while tiles
          do (let ((a (pop tiles)))
               (if (and tiles (= a (first tiles)))
                   (let ((merged (* 2 a)))
                     (pop tiles)
                     (push merged out)
                     (incf score merged))
                   (push a out))))
    (let ((result (nreverse out)))
      (values (append result
                      (make-list (- (length row) (length result))
                                 :initial-element 0))
              score))))

(defun move (board direction)
  "Slide BOARD in DIRECTION (:left :right :up :down).
Returns a fresh board, the points gained, and true if any cell changed."
  (let ((new (make-empty-board))
        (total 0)
        (changed nil))
    (dotimes (i 4)
      (let* ((coords (ecase direction
                       (:left (loop for c from 0 below 4 collect (cons i c)))
                       (:right (loop for c from 3 downto 0 collect (cons i c)))
                       (:up (loop for r from 0 below 4 collect (cons r i)))
                       (:down (loop for r from 3 downto 0 collect (cons r i)))))
             (line (mapcar (lambda (p) (aref board (car p) (cdr p))) coords)))
        (multiple-value-bind (result points) (slide-row line)
          (incf total points)
          (loop for p in coords
                for v in result
                do (setf (aref new (car p) (cdr p)) v)
                   (unless (= v (aref board (car p) (cdr p)))
                     (setf changed t))))))
    (values new total changed)))

(defun spawn-tile (board random-state)
  "Return a copy of BOARD with one new tile (2 or 4) in a random empty cell."
  (let* ((new (copy-board board))
         (empties (loop for r from 0 below 4
                        nconc (loop for c from 0 below 4
                                    when (zerop (aref board r c))
                                      collect (cons r c))))
         (cell (nth (random (length empties) random-state) empties))
         (value (if (< (random 10 random-state) 9) 2 4)))
    (setf (aref new (car cell) (cdr cell)) value)
    new))

(defun won-p (board)
  (loop for r from 0 below 4
        thereis (loop for c from 0 below 4
                      thereis (= (aref board r c) 2048))))

(defun game-over-p (board)
  (notany (lambda (direction)
            (nth-value 2 (move board direction)))
          '(:left :right :up :down)))

  (dotimes (r 4)
    (dotimes (c 4)
      (let ((v (aref board r c)))
        (if (zerop v)
            (format output "~6A" ".")
            (format output "~6D" v))))
    (terpri output))
  (format output "Score: ~D~%" score))

(defun play (&key (input *standard-input*)
                  (output *standard-output*)
                  (random-state (make-random-state t)))
  "Play 2048 as a text game reading commands from INPUT, writing to OUTPUT."
  (let* ((board (spawn-tile (spawn-tile (make-empty-board) random-state)
                            random-state))
         (score 0)
         (won nil))
    (loop
      (print-board board score output)
      (when (game-over-p board)
        (format output "Game over! Final score: ~D~%" score)
        (return))
      (let ((line (read-line input nil nil)))
        (when (or (null line)
                  (string-equal (string-trim '(#\Space #\Tab #\Return) line) "q"))
          (return))
        (let* ((key (string-trim '(#\Space #\Tab #\Return) line))
               (direction (cond ((string= key "w") :up)
                                ((string= key "a") :left)
                                ((string= key "s") :down)
                                ((string= key "d") :right)
                                (t nil))))
          (cond
            ((null direction)
             (format output "Invalid key: ~S. Use w/a/s/d to move, q to quit.~%"
                     key))
            (t
             (multiple-value-bind (new-board points changed)
                 (move board direction)
               (cond
                 ((not changed)
                  (format output "That move changed nothing.~%"))
                 (t
                  (setf board (spawn-tile new-board random-state))
                  (incf score points)
                  (when (and (not won) (won-p board))
                    (setf won t)
                    (format output "You reached 2048! You win! Keep playing if you like.~%"))))))))))
    score))

(defun slide-row (row)
  "Slide ROW toward its first element, merging once per tile.
Returns a fresh list of the same length and the points gained."
  (let ((tiles (remove 0 row))
        (out '())
        (score 0))
    (loop while tiles
          do (let ((a (pop tiles)))
               (if (and tiles (= a (first tiles)))
                   (let ((merged (* 2 a)))
                     (pop tiles)
                     (push merged out)
                     (incf score merged))
                   (push a out))))
    (let ((result (nreverse out)))

                                 :initial-element 0))

  "Slide BOARD in DIRECTION (:left :right :up :down).

  (let ((new (make-empty-board))

        (changed nil))

                       (:left (loop for c from 0 below 4 collect (cons i c)))
                       (:right (loop for c from 3 downto 0 collect (cons i c)))
                       (:up (loop for r from 0 below 4 collect (cons r i)))
                       (:down (loop for r from 3 downto 0 collect (cons r i)))))

(in-package :game-2048-tests)

;;; Helpers

(defun board-from-rows (rows)
  (let ((b (make-array '(4 4) :initial-element 0)))
    (loop for row in rows
          for r from 0
          do (loop for v in row
                   for c from 0
                   do (setf (aref b r c) v)))
    b))

(defun board-rows (board)
  (loop for r from 0 below 4
        collect (loop for c from 0 below 4 collect (aref board r c))))

(defun contains (needle haystack)
  (and (search needle haystack) t))

(defun run-play (input-string)
  "Run PLAY on INPUT-STRING with a fixed random state; return the transcript."
  (let ((out (make-string-output-stream)))
    (play :input (make-string-input-stream input-string)
          :output out
          :random-state (make-random-state nil))
    (get-output-stream-string out)))

(defun slide-result (row)
  "The list of values slide-row returns for ROW: (cells score)."
  (multiple-value-bind (cells score) (slide-row row)
    (list cells score)))

(defun move-result (rows direction)
  "The list of values move returns: (rows points changed)."
  (multiple-value-bind (new points changed)
      (move (board-from-rows rows) direction)
    (list (board-rows new) points changed)))

# Tests for `lisp-check --test`

`lisp-check --test` loads the compiled file, and loading runs every top-level
`tester` assertion in it. Write test files in the shape of
`examples/count-words-tests.lisp`, which passes `lisp-check --test`. It starts:

```lisp
(eval-when (:compile-toplevel :load-toplevel :execute)
  (require :tester))

(defpackage :count-words-tests
  (:use :cl :util.test))

(in-package :count-words-tests)
```

then defines `count-words` and `first-word`, and ends with the assertions:

```lisp
(test 0 (count-words ""))
(test 3 (count-words "  read  compile test "))
(test '(0 1 2) (mapcar #'count-words '("" "lisp" "a b")) :test #'equal)
(test "read" (first-word "  read compile") :test #'string=)
(test-error (first-word "   "))
```

- Name the file `NAME-tests.lisp`.
- Start with the `eval-when` / `require` form, so the `util.test` package
  exists when the file compiles.
- Put each assertion at top level. `lisp-check` counts top-level assertions
  only; assertions inside `with-tests` give `no tester assertions ran`.
- `(test WANTED FORM)` compares with `eql`. Compare strings with
  `:test #'string=` and lists with `:test #'equal`.
- `test` fails with `additional value were returned from test form` when
  FORM returns more than one value, as `gethash`, `parse-integer` and
  `read-line` do. Keep only the first value:
  `(test 2 (values (gethash "and" *counts*)))`.
- A tests file for a project uses the project's package:
  `(:use :cl :util.test :tally)`. `lisp-check` loads the project's `.asd`
  first (lisp-project skill).
- `(test-error FORM)` passes when FORM signals a `simple-error`, which
  `(error "...")` does. For another condition class add
  `:condition-type 'CLASS`. Test errors your code signals itself: compiled
  code may skip type checks, so `(car 1)` can return garbage instead of
  signalling `type-error`.

  (:use :common-lisp :util.test :game-2048))

(in-package :game-2048-tests)

;;; Helpers (all return a single value)

(defun board-from-rows (rows)
  (let ((b (make-array '(4 4) :initial-element 0)))
    (loop for row in rows
          for r from 0
          do (loop for v in row
                   for c from 0
                   do (setf (aref b r c) v)))
    b))

(defun board-rows (board)
  (loop for r from 0 below 4
        collect (loop for c from 0 below 4 collect (aref board r c))))

(defun contains (needle haystack)
  (and (search needle haystack) t))

(defun run-play (input-string)
  "Run PLAY on INPUT-STRING with a fixed random state; return the transcript."
  (let ((out (make-string-output-stream)))
    (play :input (make-string-input-stream input-string)
          :output out
          :random-state (make-random-state nil))
    (get-output-stream-string out)))

(defun slide-cells (row)
  (values (slide-row row)))

(defun slide-points (row)
  (nth-value 1 (slide-row row)))

(defun move-cells (rows direction)
  (board-rows (values (move (board-from-rows rows) direction))))

(defun move-points (rows direction)
  (nth-value 1 (move (board-from-rows rows) direction)))

(defun move-changed (rows direction)
  (nth-value 2 (move (board-from-rows rows) direction)))

(defun spawned-cells (rows)
